# PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE (PID)

Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) refers to bacterial infection of the upper female reproductive tract. Likely bacterial pathogens include Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, anaerobes, enteric Gram-negative rods, and Streptococcus agalactiae. PID should be considered in sexually active women with pelvic tenderness and signs of lower genital tract inflammation. Signs and symptoms may be mild or non-specific, and providers should have a low threshold to initiate treatment. All women who are diagnosed with acute PID should be tested for N. gonorrohoeae, C. trachomatis, and HIV. Male sex partners of patients with PID should be examined and treated (see below) if they had sexual contact within the 60 days before onset of the patient's symptoms.

Judge severity of infection based on clinical signs and symptoms, including blood pressure, pulse, mental status, and degree of fever.

## Outpatient

## mild to moderate disease

Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x 1 dose ($) [M]
<AND>
doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14 days ($) [DI]
<OPTIONAL> metronidazole 500 mg PO BID ($) [DI]

## For patients who cannot take ceftriaxone and doxycycline, call ID

## Treatment of sex partner who is a veteran

Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x 1 dose ($) [M] < AND > doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 7 days ($) [DI]
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x 1 dose ($) [M] < AND > azithromycin 1 gm PO x 1 dose

Treat for both Chlamydia and Gonorrhea
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once ($) [M] < AND > doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 7 days ($) [DI]
< OR >
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once ($) [M] < AND > azithromycin 1 gm PO once ($) [M]

## Treatment for severe disease

Treat for 14 days.
Ceftriaxone 1 gm IV q24h [M] < AND > doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h [DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q12h [DI]
